C1: Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement and the Chemistry of Carbon Removal

Quality checked lesson

Explain the chemistry idea behind ocean alkalinity enhancement, the measurement problem, and why research must move slowly.

C1 pre-reading primer

Energy system extension

Use these cards to connect the technical parts of the lesson without making the main reading too heavy.

Alkalinity

Water capacity to neutralize acid

It affects how much carbon seawater can hold.

Bicarbonate

A dissolved carbon form

It is one way carbon can be stored in seawater.

Additionality

Extra removal beyond the baseline

It prevents counting carbon that would have been absorbed anyway.

Durability

How long storage lasts

Short storage may not help climate goals enough.

Step

What Happens

Risk Or Limit

Add alkalinity

Minerals or electrochemical bases increase seawater alkalinity.

Local chemistry can change too quickly.

Air-sea exchange

The ocean may absorb more atmospheric carbon dioxide.

Wind, mixing, and baseline variability complicate measurement.

Store carbon

Carbon shifts into dissolved bicarbonate and carbonate forms.

Durability depends on circulation and chemistry.

Monitor effects

Scientists track carbon, pH, organisms, and community impacts.

Weak monitoring can create false confidence.

C1 analysis prompts

  • Explain additionality using a simple budget analogy.
  • Name two reasons ocean carbon removal needs community engagement.
  • Compare enhanced weathering and electrochemical OAE in one paragraph.
